discrepancies.why: The building is leased to one operator, so occupancy of the lease itself is 100% and income is that operator's covenant. Behind the lease the operator sub-lets 77 of 90 units (85.6%) and collects about AED 5,108,000 a year against the AED 5,976,000 it pays, while bearing the running costs: the rent is supported by the operator, not earned by the units. That is covenant risk. At expiry, or if the operator fails, income falls to what the sub-tenancies earn. Whether the operator is related to the seller is a separate question, decided only on stated evidence. Review: All of the headline income (AED 5.98m, 100% leased) comes from one operator that the OM itself says is in the seller's group. The rent was set by a connected party, not by the market. It is not an arm's-length covenant. The 'guaranteed' rent is only as good as that operator's ability to pay. The operator sub-lets the units and the code-parsed rent roll shows it collects less from sub-tenants than it pays. The 5-year term ends June 2029. After that, income reverts to market rent, and the master tenant could stop paying if the seller group leaves the operator under-funded. The 'no vacancy risk' claim moves the risk onto the operator's covenant. It does not remove it.

discrepancies.why: The OM presents the building as hands-free with a guaranteed 8.25% ROI on asking price. That figure is gross rent over price. The tenancy schedule shows the landlord still bears insurance, structural repairs, the reserve fund and, per the landlord statement, master community charges, audit and legal costs and an asset management fee, with 5% VAT not recoverable. Net yield will be lower than the headline, and the OM states no net income. The word 'guaranteed' rests only on the related-party operator's covenant, and no security is described.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Rebuild net operating income from the landlord statement, after confirming the figures are actuals and not budget. Compute yield on asking price plus acquisition costs. Request details of any guarantee or security backing the master lease rent.

notices.text: Cheque profile: 39% of rent on 1-2 cheques, 38% of rent on 3-4 cheques, 23% of rent on 6 or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
Master lease, operator accounts and ownership, and the novation terms of the sub-tenancies at expiry.

Behind the lease the operator sub-lets 77 of 90 units (85.6%) and collects about AED 5,108,000 a year against the AED 5,976,000 it pays, while bearing the running costs: the rent is supported by the operator, not earned by the units. That is covenant risk. At expiry, or if the operator fails, income falls to what the sub-tenancies earn. Whether the operator is related to the seller is a separate question, decided only on stated evidence. Review: All of the headline income (AED 5.98m, 100% leased) comes from one operator that the OM itself says is in the seller's group. The rent was set by a connected party, not by the market. It is not an arm's-length covenant. The 'guaranteed' rent is only as good as that operator's ability to pay. The operator sub-lets the units and the code-parsed rent roll shows it collects less from sub-tenants than it pays. The 5-year term ends June 2029. After that, income reverts to market rent, and the master tenant could stop paying if the seller group leaves the operator under-funded. The 'no vacancy risk' claim moves the risk onto the operator's covenant. It does not remove it.

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Decline**: The income rests on a master lease to an operator that the OM says is in the seller's group, and the mandate has a hard filter against master leases to a related party. Every other hard filter passes. Nothing else changes the outcome.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Silverline Residences, Dubai Silicon Oasis. It has 90 units [[om.unit_count]] and was completed in 2018 [[deal.completion_year]].
- **Price:** The asking price is AED 72.5m [[deal.asking_price_aed]]. That is AED 770 per sq ft [[om.price_psf_stated]] on BUA, or AED 1,013 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA.
- **Income:** One operator, Silverline Homes Management L.L.C, pays a master lease rent of AED 6.0m [[rr.master_lease_rent_aed]] until 30 June 2029 [[rr.master_lease_end]]. The operator sub-lets 77 [[rr.let_units]] of 90 [[rr.unit_count]] units, which is 86% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] occupancy by units. The sub-tenants pay AED 5.1m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] in place, and 13 units [[rr.vacant_units]] are vacant.

## Returns
For reference only; not decisive.

| Metric | Result | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Unlevered IRR, pre-tax | 2.0% [[uw.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]] | 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] target |
| Unlevered equity multiple, pre-tax | 1.09x [[uw.unlevered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | 1.30x [[mandate.target_unlevered_equity_multiple.threshold]] target |
| Entry yield on price | 7.4% [[uw.entry_yield_on_price]] | none |
| Exit yield | 7.6% [[uw.exit_yield]] | none |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 7.0% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | 6.0% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] minimum |

Year-1 NOI is AED 5.4m [[uw.noi_year1]]. The deal misses both return targets and passes only the yield-on-cost minimum.

Levered returns are secondary. Levered IRR is a loss of 1.8% a year [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]], the levered multiple is 0.92x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]], and Year-1 DSCR is 1.52x [[uw.dscr_year1]].

The OM's headline yield is 8.2% [[om.yield_stated]] on asking price. On the buyer's basis (Year-1 NOI on price plus acquisition costs) it is 7.0% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. The gap is negative: the buyer's yield sits 1.3 points [[uw.om_yield.gap_vs_stated]] below the OM's figure.

## What would make it fail
The deal is declined, so one line is enough. When the master lease ends in June 2029 [[rr.master_lease_end]], or if the operator fails, income falls to what the sub-tenancies earn. The operator already pays AED 868k [[disc.master_lease_related_party.impact_aed]] more than it collects from them.

## Discrepancies
1. **Master lease to the seller's group (high).** The OM says the operator is in the seller's group, so the rent was set by a connected party, not by the market. The screen relied on the master-lease rent to expiry, then on the sub-tenancies. The operator pays AED 6.0m [[rr.master_lease_rent_aed]] but collects less from sub-tenants, and it bears the running costs. The "guaranteed" rent is only as good as that operator's covenant. The overstatement is AED 868k [[disc.master_lease_related_party.impact_aed]].
2. **The headline yield is gross (medium).** The OM's 8.2% [[om.yield_stated]] is gross rent on asking price, before acquisition costs of 6.2% [[uw.acquisition_costs_pct_of_price]]. On price plus costs the same income gives 7.8% [[uw.om_yield.stated_income_on_total_cost]], which is 0.5 points [[disc.yield_excludes_acquisition_costs.impact_ratio]] lower. The OM also says the operator pays all running costs. The landlord still bears insurance, structural repairs, the reserve fund and other charges, and VAT is not recoverable. The OM states no net income. I count the impact once.

Lower-severity items are not discussed.

## Checks before diligence
- Get the master lease, the operator's accounts and ownership, and the seller's ownership. Confirm in writing whether the operator is related to the seller.
- Rebuild NOI from the landlord statement, after confirming the figures are actuals and not budget.
- Ask the broker to restate the yield on total cost. Ask for details of any guarantee or security behind the master lease rent.
- Cheque profile: 23% [[notice.cheque_profile]] of rent is on six or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search, including freehold status, single title and buyer eligibility.
- Dubai Municipality completion certificate.
- Affection plan and permitted use.
- Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
- Civil Defence and fire-safety certificates, and cladding compliance.
- Novation terms of the sub-tenancies at master lease expiry.

## Assumptions
The returns rest on the firm's house view, not on market evidence for this building. The exit yield is 7.6% [[uw.exit_yield]]. Market rent falls 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1 and 1% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2, then rises 2% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. Structural vacancy is 5.0% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] and collection loss is 1.0% [[assume.collection_loss]]. Debt is capped at 45% [[assume.max_ltv]] LTV and sized to a 1.40x [[assume.sizing_dscr]] DSCR. The statement omitted maintenance, common utilities, and security and cleaning, so mandate defaults fill them, along with marketing and leasing. Year-1 operating costs are AED 555k [[uw.operating_costs_year1]] against AED 364k [[opex.total_expenses_aed]] on the statement.
